text:
rachel: Heads-up: found a hairy onboarding inconsistency that keeps hitting Windows users. README has instructions for exporting env vars using POSIX `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...`, but the Windows PowerShell snippet in the same file shows `$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = 'sk-REPLACE'` separately in a different section. People copy the POSIX line into PowerShell and then wonder why the SDK can't read the key.

vik: Ugh, cross-platform docs drift. Which README is this?

rachel: examples/quickstart/README.md — onboarding section. Current top-of-file shows a small "Set env" box with POSIX only, then a few paragraphs later we have a PowerShell example, but they use a different env name there: `REDWOOD_KEY` (old). So two problems: wrong env name and inconsistent instruction placement (users only see the first box).

ash: That's nasty. Windows users often just follow the top-most codeblock. If it's POSIX-only they copy into PowerShell which sets a local variable that doesn't persist across new shells. Also the legacy `REDWOOD_KEY` vs `REDWOOD_API_KEY` will cause SDK constructors that read REDWOOD_API_KEY to fail.

rachel: Proposed minimal fix: centralize the env var instructions into a single platform-aware block at the top, show POSIX, PowerShell, and cmd variants, all using REDWOOD_API_URL and REDWOOD_API_KEY, and add a one-liner note: "On Windows, use PowerShell or set machine/user env via system settings for persistent values."

Suggested snippet to replace current scattered ones:

```bash
# macOS / Linux (bash/zsh)
export REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.ai
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-REPLACE_ME
```

```powershell
# PowerShell (persist for current session)
$env:REDWOOD_API_URL = 'https://api.redwood.ai'
$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = 'sk-REPLACE_ME'
```

```cmd
:: Windows cmd.exe
set REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.ai
set REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-REPLACE_ME
```

vik: LGTM. Also recommend adding a tiny note that CLI helpers (our redwoodctl) accept `--api-key` flag so users who don't want to set envs can pass the key directly when running a single command. That avoids permanent env setup mistakes.

ash: One more gotcha: our Node quickstart snippet does `const client = new RedwoodClient()` and expects it to auto-read process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, but our Python quickstart example constructs `RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))` in that file, which still references the old var name and defeats the centralized env doc. We need parity.

rachel: I'll open a docs PR to: 1) centralize env instructions at the top, 2) rename all REDWOOD_KEY -> REDWOOD_API_KEY, 3) add the CLI `--api-key` example, and 4) run docs-lint. I'll ping @vik for a review and ask @ash to sanity-check Windows formatting.

docs-bot: created issue #4010 to track cross-platform env parity and CLI flag example.

winbot: FYI: Windows users report copying the POSIX command into PowerShell then running `node sample.js` still shows 401 because PowerShell requires different quoting in CI agents; consider adding a troubleshooting FAQ entry: "I set the env but get 401" with steps to print env in the same shell: `node -e "console.log(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY)"`.

vik: Great idea. Add that troubleshooting snippet and a one-liner to the onboarding file. Also run a quick smoke test in CI that runs the Node sample in a PowerShell runner to catch regressions.

rachel: Thanks team 44d I'll open the PR and include the CI smoke test. These small platform mismatches are a silent onboarding tax. :disappointed_relieved:"
